## Goal

One supervisor per home that hosts and clients can always find, that survives races, crashes and stale state, and that owns the ledger and every child process.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| RT-06 | One instance per home: a host-spawned process over stdio or a standalone daemon the CLI attaches to over the home socket; racing starters converge on one supervisor and stale sockets are recovered | I, C | 16 racing starters converge on one supervisor; stale socket recovered; `mostra host` over stdio and attach over socket both pass the protocol suite |
| RT-07 | macOS and Linux are supported; on any other platform every entry point fails closed with a clear diagnostic (Windows is out of v1.0) | I | macOS and Linux CI legs green; simulated Windows platform fails closed with MOSTRA_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED before touching the home |
| RT-09 | Every child process runs in its own process group, is recorded with PID and start time, and is reaped after a supervisor crash, including grandchildren such as demo servers and PTY programs | I | SIGKILL the supervisor with demo and PTY grandchildren running; next start reaps them by recorded PID and start time |
| HO-02 | A versioned, language-neutral host protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0, stdio required) with capability negotiation and version refusal | C | Revision negotiation picks highest common; unsupported revision refused with the code (protocol suite) |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- the supervisor entry and home resolution;
- the socket bind and attach, stale takeover, `mostra host` over stdio;
- the protocol server with `mostra/initialize` negotiation and revision refusal;
- the ledger module (better-sqlite3, WAL, full sync, migrations with backup, integrity check);
- the process manager (process groups, `child` table, reaping after a crash, IPC);
- the unsupported-platform gate;
- `instance/status`.

Design detail for this package:

- Home resolution order: `--home`, `MOSTRA_HOME`, SDK option, platform default; create 0700.
- Socket path in the per-user runtime directory with a hashed home name (104-byte limit on macOS); accept both `EADDRINUSE` and `EEXIST` on bind races (prototype finding).
- Takeover mutex: atomic `mkdir`, owner PID and timestamp inside, broken after 30 s when the owner is gone.
- `mostra host` over newline-delimited stdio and the socket server share one protocol dispatcher; port callbacks bind to the registering connection.
- Ledger module: better-sqlite3, WAL, `synchronous=FULL`, migrations with file backup, integrity check, `MOSTRA_HOME_TOO_NEW`; the only writer.
- Process manager: spawn in a new process group, record PID and start time, reap on start, IPC with typed messages, exit on IPC disconnect in children.
- Platform gate before touching the home (D35).

## Out of scope

- The gateway (WP-05), builder (WP-03), workers (WP-08).

## Acceptance evidence

integration tests for racing starters (one supervisor), stale-socket recovery, supervisor SIGKILL with grandchildren reaped, version negotiation and refusal, migration with backup, and the Windows gate (simulated platform) (FAILURE_MODEL §2, §3).

Also: `pnpm check` green (from WP-01 on), diff reviewed, evidence matrix rows updated, docs and AGENTS.md current, progress report written after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Start-time reading differs on macOS and Linux (`ps -o lstart` vs `/proc/<pid>/stat`): test both in CI.

## Handoff

A protocol server with negotiation, a ledger with migrations, and a process manager every later child uses.
